answer: An agent economy can bind voting power to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is locked for a cooling-off period before an identity can influence a shared reputation score. Splitting one stake across a hundred umber or zephyr personas does not create more total influence, while acquiring extra stake ties up capital and exposes it to slashing if those identities coordinate fraudulently. The garden of identities is therefore costly to fake at scale, though stake alone cannot stop a wealthy attacker.
